newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer says dollar level not due to EMU worries.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer says dollar level not due to EMU worries.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said on Tuesday that the German central bank would "do everything" to hold onto the mark's strength and transfer it to a strong euro.

Tietmeyer, speaking at the Global 24 conference, also said he believed the current strength of the dollar was due more to a correction from recent weakness and did not generally reflect expectations for a weak euro when launched in January 1999.
"I would not like to talk about the weak DM but about a strong dollar," Tietmeyer, speaking in English, told the conference.
"I think developments on foreign exchange markets are a real correction of the revaluation of the exchange rate developments in the last years," Tietmeyer said.
"I do not see it now as an indicator that there is any less confidence that the euro will be a strong currency," he said.
He also said, "I do not see that there is a weakness in the mark. I can tell you that we will do everything to hold the mark as strong as it is and transfer it into the then hopefully strong euro."
Tietmeyer said it was "very important" that conditions for a stable euro be met for its start in January 1999 and that preparatory work for EMU keep going in the right direction.
"We have to create confidence," Tietmeyer said. "This is the most important thing to the transfer, the credibility of the European currency has gained in the last years."

"I think there is a good chance but we have to be aware that this means really following a sound, sustainable policy," he said. "I think we have a chance but not everything is already done. A lot of things have to be done, especially in some countries in Europe."
Tietmeyer said he hoped European countries would succeed in bringing budget projects under control on a sustainable basis and improve the functionality of markets.
